title: Tic-tac-toe judge
prompt:
The starter reads a tic-tac-toe board into `board` as one line of nine characters, row by row: `X`, `O`, or `.` for an empty cell. The input `XOX.OX.O.` is this board:

```text
X O X
. O X
. O .
```

Print `X wins` or `O wins` when a row, a column, or a diagonal holds three of the same mark. When no line is complete, print `keep playing` if any cell is still empty, or `draw` if the board is full.

The board is a two-dimensional array stored one row after another (row-major order), one byte per cell, so the cell in row r, column c is the byte at `board + r * 3 + c`. The boards come from real games, so at most one player has a complete line.

## what is checked

- one line with the verdict
- the program exits cleanly
- cells are read from memory one byte at a time (`ldrb` present)
- your program also runs on boards you do not see: wins along a row, a column and each diagonal, a full board with a winner, a full board without one, and an empty board
starter:
// read a tic-tac-toe board and say who won
define(fp, x29)
define(lr, x30)

define(board_r, x19)

.data
fmt_in:     .string "%9s"
fmt_win:    .string "%c wins\n"
msg_draw:   .string "draw\n"
msg_open:   .string "keep playing\n"

.bss
.align 4
board:      .skip 16                        // 9 cells row by row, then the zero byte

.text
        .balign 4
        .global main
main:
        stp     fp, lr, [sp, -16]!
        mov     fp, sp

        ldr     x0, =fmt_in                 // read the nine cells as one word
        ldr     x1, =board
        bl      scanf
        ldr     board_r, =board

        // TODO: the cell in row r, column c is the byte at
        // board_r + r * 3 + c. Check the three rows, the three columns
        // and the two diagonals. If a line holds three X or three O,
        // print that mark with fmt_win. Otherwise print msg_open when
        // any cell is still '.', or msg_draw when the board is full.

        mov     w0, 0
        ldp     fp, lr, [sp], 16
        ret
